newsitem.title: USA: Fast tactics slow spread of U.S. hog herd virus.
newsitem.headline: Fast tactics slow spread of U.S. hog herd virus.

text.p: Quick adoption of strict herd management practices and the use of vaccines has slowed the spread of an acute viral disease that surfaced last fall in segments of the U.S. hog herd, industry officials said.
Porcine Reproductive and Respiratory Syndrome (PRRS) causes abortions and respiratory ailments in hogs.
"Management solutions appear to be working," said John McNutt, chairman of the National Pork Producers Council's swine health committee.

In an interview during the NPPC's World Pork Expo here, McNutt said the industry has spent hundreds of thousands of dollars to find a cure for the disease, which caused a rise in hog abortions and deaths late last year.
One successful strategy has been to keep hogs arriving on farms separated from the main herd for about 60 days, versus the standard 21-day separation.
McNutt said that provided time to determine if the hogs were infected and reduced the spread of the disease.
NPPC announced during the Pork Expo that it and the USDA's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service will cooperate on a study of the outbreaks and of herds previously affected.
